rows.name: dir?
rows.notes: Not defaulted, deliberately: left unset the resolved page direction governs, so a subtree inside an RTL region inherits instead of being reset to `ltr`.

rows.name: count
rows.notes: Total number of paginated items. Required.

rows.name: page?
rows.notes: Controlled. 1-based.

rows.name: pageSize?
rows.notes: Controlled.

rows.name: siblingCount?
rows.notes: Pages adjacent to the current one, on each side. Default 1; 0 is allowed.

rows.name: boundaryCount?
rows.notes: Pages pinned at each end. Default 1.

rows.name: type?
rows.notes: `"button"` (default) or `"link"` — a crawlable pagination, one href per page.

rows.name: getPageUrl?
rows.notes: Required when `type === "link"`.

rows.name: intents?
rows.notes: Where LT/RT arrive from. `null` when the app runs no input system.

rows.name: onPageChange?
rows.notes: Also fired *correctively*: a `count` that shrinks under the current page, or a page held out of bounds by a controlled consumer, is re-clamped by the machine's watch — the same re-settle policy as `tabs.syncTriggers`.

rows.name: prevLabel?
rows.notes: What the previous-page control shows. Content, never its name: the machine writes `aria-label="previous page"` whatever is in here, so an inline SVG costs nothing and an empty control is a drawn one rather than a blank.

rows.name: nextLabel?
rows.notes: The same, for the next-page control.

rows.name: renderItem?
rows.notes: Replaces the CHILDREN of a page cell, never the cell. `defaults` is what the layer would have rendered — the page number — and it is handed over so that **decorating** is the cheapest thing to do. Replacing it is the consumer's to do and costs nothing this time: the cell's accessible name is `aria-label` on the button, written by the machine, so a cell whose children are a spinner is still "page 4". That is a difference from every other `render*` in the composed layer, and it is worth stating rather than assuming.

rows.name: rootLabel?
rows.notes: Defaults to `"pagination"`.

rows.name: prevTriggerLabel?
rows.notes: Defaults to `"previous page"`.

rows.name: nextTriggerLabel?
rows.notes: Defaults to `"next page"`.

rows.name: itemLabel?
rows.notes: Defaults to `` `page ${page}` ``.

rows.name: item?
rows.notes: Applied to EVERY cell, hence no `page` — it identifies the cell — and no `id` **or IDREF**: one id repeated down a bar is a broken reference per cell, and one `aria-labelledby` repeated gives every cell the same name, which no dangling-IDREF check can see because the id it points at does resolve. `ref` goes for the same reason: a single ref held by N cells holds the last one.

rows.name: ellipsis?
rows.notes: Applied to EVERY gap; `index` is the machine's, one per gap.

rows.name: index
rows.notes: Where this ellipsis sits in the page model — presentation only.

rows.name: root
rows.notes: PaginationRoot

rows.name: item
rows.notes: PaginationItem

rows.name: ellipsis
rows.notes: PaginationEllipsis

rows.notes: PaginationPrevTrigger

rows.notes: PaginationNextTrigger
